VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

> General information based on the binding VŠE Study and Examination Rules (*Studijní a zkušební řád VŠE*). Always verify your individual study plan and credit status in InSIS under **Student's Portal → Check of Study Plan**, or consult your faculty Study Department.

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

## 1. Credit Requirements: How Many Credits Do I Need?

### Standard Full-Time Load
- **Per Semester:** The standard study load is **30 ECTS credits** per semester.
- **Per Academic Year:** **60 ECTS credits** per academic year (two teaching semesters).
- **Total for Bachelor’s Degree:** **180 ECTS credits** (standard 3 years / 6 semesters).
- **Total for Master’s Degree:** **120 ECTS credits** (standard 2 years / 4 semesters).

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

### Minimum Credit Thresholds (To Avoid Expulsion / Study Termination)
To remain actively enrolled at VŠE, you must satisfy two critical threshold checkpoints:
1. **First-Semester Absolute Minimum:**
   - By the end of your **first semester** at VŠE, you must earn **at least 9 ECTS credits** (or 9 credit vouchers converted).
   - If you earn fewer than 9 credits in your first semester, your studies are **immediately terminated** by the Dean for failure to make required academic progress.
2. **Ongoing Semesters Progression Threshold (20 Credits Rule):**
   - For every active (non-interrupted) semester, your cumulative earned credits must satisfy the formula:
     `Cumulative Minimum Credits >= 20 x number of active semesters`
     - **After Semester 1:** At least 9 credits to avoid expulsion; **20 credits** to stay on track without voucher deduction penalties.
     - **After Semester 2:** At least **40 credits** accumulated.
     - **After Semester 3:** At least **60 credits** accumulated.
     - **After Semester 4:** At least **80 credits** accumulated.
     - **After Semester 5:** At least **100 credits** accumulated.
     - **After Semester 6:** At least **120 credits** (or 180 to graduate for Bachelor's).
   - If your accumulated credits fall below `20 x active semesters`, the system automatically subtracts credit vouchers equal to the missing credits as a penalty.

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

### Maximum Credits per Semester: Can I Take More Than 30 Credits?
- **No Upper Cap:** There is **no administrative limit** preventing you from enrolling in 35, 40, or more ECTS credits in a single semester.
- As long as you have sufficient credit vouchers in your account, meet course prerequisites, and your weekly timetable has no overlapping conflicts, you may enroll in extra courses.

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

## 2. The VŠE Credit Voucher System (Kreditní poukázky)

VŠE uses a virtual currency called **Credit Vouchers** (*Kreditní poukázky*) alongside ECTS credits to measure your study budget:

### Voucher Allotment (1.2× Safety Buffer)
Upon initial enrollment, every student receives a voucher pool equal to **120%** of their degree requirement:
- **Bachelor’s Students:** **216 vouchers** (180 for standard curriculum + 36 reserve vouchers = 20% safety margin).
- **Master’s Students:** **144 vouchers** (120 for standard curriculum + 24 reserve vouchers = 20% safety margin).

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

### How Vouchers Work
- **1 ECTS Credit = 1 Voucher:** Enrolling in a 6-credit course deducts 6 vouchers from your active voucher balance.
- **Passing a Course:** Successfully completing the course converts the deducted vouchers into permanent earned ECTS credits.
- **Failing a Course:** If you fail a course, the deducted vouchers are **lost permanently**. You gain 0 ECTS credits, and your reserve voucher pool is depleted.
- **Voucher Penalty Deduction:** If at the end of a semester your cumulative credits are less than `20 x active semesters`, additional vouchers are deducted from your account.

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

### Study Termination Due to Insufficient Vouchers
- At the end of each semester, InSIS checks your remaining voucher balance against the remaining ECTS credits needed to graduate.
- **Termination Rule:** If your remaining vouchers are **strictly less than the remaining credits needed to complete your degree**, your studies are terminated by law, because it is mathematically impossible to register for all required remaining courses.

## 3. Course Types and Repeating Failed Courses

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

## 3. Course Types and Repeating Failed Courses

### Course Categories in Your Study Plan
1. **Compulsory Courses (`oP` – Povinné předměty, Class I):**
   - Mandatory for all students in your programme or major.
   - **Failing a Compulsory Course:** You **must re-enroll** in the course in the next semester it is offered, which consumes another batch of vouchers from your reserve pool.
   - **Maximum Enrollments:** A compulsory course can only be enrolled a maximum of **two times**. If you fail a compulsory course on its second enrollment, your studies are terminated.
2. **Minor Specialization Courses (`sP` compulsory Class I / `sV` selective Class II):**
   - Belong to a Minor Specialization (*vedlejší specializace*).
   - If you fail an elective `sV` course, the vouchers are lost, and you may choose a different eligible `sV` course in future semesters.
3. **Faculty & Free Electives (`fV` / `cV` / `oV`, Class II):**
   - Faculty electives, university-wide electives, foreign language courses, sports, or International Week courses.
   - If failed, you lose the vouchers, but you do not need to repeat the same course; you can choose an alternative elective.
4. **Minor Specialization (*Vedlejší specializace*):**
   - Standard Czech Master's curricula and selected programmes include a structured **30 ECTS Minor Specialization** concluding with a minor comprehensive exam. Requirements vary for English-taught Master's programmes (such as ISM), so verify your programme plan in InSIS (**Check of Study Plan**) or with your faculty Study Department.

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

## 4. Grading System and Exam Retakes

### VŠE Grading Scale (Including `4+`)
VŠE uses an inverted Czech grading scale with a distinctive **`4+`** conditional-fail grade:
| Grade | Czech Term | Meaning | Percentage Scale | ECTS Equivalent |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1** | Výborně | Excellent | 90–100% | A |
| **2** | Velmi dobře | Very Good | 75–89% | B |
| **3** | Dobře | Good | 60–74% | C – E |
| **4+** | Nevyhověl s možností opravy | Conditional Fail (one retake right) | 50–59% | FX (Retake permitted) |
| **4** | Nevyhověl | Definitive Fail | 0–49% | F (No credits gained) |

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

### Exam Retakes (`4+` Rule — *Opravný termín*)
- Under the VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ), a student who receives a **`4+`** grade (typically **50–59%**) is entitled to **one retake attempt** (*opravný termín*) on an available exam date within the same examination period.
- **Key Restrictions on `4+`:**
  - `4+` **cannot be awarded twice in succession** for the same course.
  - `4+` **cannot be awarded on the last exam date** of the period (because no remaining date exists for a retake), so students are strongly advised not to leave their first attempt until the final exam slot.
  - If you do not use your retake before the exam period closes, `4+` **automatically converts to a definitive `4` (Fail)**.
- A definitive grade of **`4`** (below 50% or failing the `4+` retake) yields 0 ECTS and permanently consumes the course's credit vouchers; you must re-enroll in a future semester if it is a compulsory course (`oP`). Always confirm course-specific assessment rules in the InSIS syllabus and with your faculty Study Department.

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

## 5. Study Interruption (Přerušení studia)
- **What it is:** An official pause/freeze of your university studies.
- **Eligibility:** You can apply to interrupt your studies after earning the minimum first-semester credits, or anytime for serious documented medical, personal, or maternity reasons.
- **How to Apply:** Submit an electronic application via InSIS under **Student's Portal → Contact Study Department / Applications**.
- ⚠️ **Critical Warning for Visa Students (Non-EU):**
  - During study interruption, **you lose your legal student status**.
  - VŠE is legally required to notify the Czech Foreign Police and Ministry of the Interior (OAMP/MVČR), which may invalidate your student residence permit or visa. Always consult the VŠE International Office before applying to interrupt!

title: VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers
text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

## 6. Transfer and Recognition of Previous Credits (Uznávání předmětů)
- Courses completed at another university or in previous VŠE studies may be recognized by your faculty.
- **Conditions:**
  - Only courses evaluated with grade **1 (Excellent)**, **2 (Very Good)**, or **Credited (*započteno*)** are eligible for recognition — grade **3 (Good)** is generally not eligible.
  - Eligibility time limits (commonly **3 calendar years** for prior VŠE studies) and syllabus equivalence rules are set by faculty Dean's Directives — confirm exact rules with your faculty Study Department.
- **How to Apply:** Submit an official recognition request via InSIS with your official transcript of records and syllabus to the Vice-Dean for Study Affairs.

text:
VŠE Study Regulations, ECTS credits, minimum semester requirements and credit vouchers

## 7. How to Check Your Academic Standing in InSIS
1. Log in to InSIS at https://insis.vse.cz/.
2. Go to **Student's Portal** (*Portál studenta*).
3. Click on **Check of Study Plan** (*Kontrola plánu*) to view your completed ECTS, pending courses, and graduation progress.
4. Click on **E-study record / Vouchers** (*Zápisové listy / Kreditní poukázky*) to check your exact remaining credit voucher balance.
5. If in doubt, contact your faculty Study Department (*Studijní oddělení*).

title: Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules
text:
Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules

## 1. Non-EU / Non-EEA Students: Visa vs. Long-Term Residence Permit
Students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland staying in the Czech Republic for more than 90 days must apply **before arrival** at a territorially competent Czech Embassy or Consulate for one of two study authorizations:
- **Long-Term Visa for the Purpose of Studies (*Vízum k pobytu nad 90 dnů za účelem studia*):** Issued for up to 1 year; renewable in the Czech Republic as a long-term residence permit.
- **Long-Term Residence Permit for the Purpose of Studies (*Povolení k dlouhodobému pobytu za účelem studia*):** Issued directly for accredited university degree programmes and exchange studies; requires post-arrival biometric card collection at MOI OAMP in Prague.
- **Student Facilitation Programme (*Režim student*):** Degree and exchange students admitted to VŠE may be nominated by the VŠE Admission Office / International Office for priority embassy appointment scheduling where applicable.

title: Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules
text:
Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules

## 2. Core Documents Required for Czech Study Visa / Residence Permit
1. **Valid Travel Passport** (valid at least 3 months beyond intended stay, with at least 2 blank pages) and passport-sized photographs.
2. **Official Confirmation of Study (*Potvrzení o přijetí ke studiu / Potvrzení o studiu*):** Issued by VŠE (in Czech) confirming enrollment in an accredited study programme.
3. **Proof of Accommodation (*Doklad o zajištění ubytování*):**
   - **VŠE Dormitory (SÚZ / ISKaM):** Official electronically signed accommodation confirmation issued via ISKaM (https://iskam-web.vse.cz/) after paying the booking deposit (*kauce*).
   - **Private Flat / Apartment:** Signed lease contract (*Nájemní smlouva*) or official Accommodation Confirmation form with an officially verified signature of the property owner.

title: Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules
text:
Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules

4. **Proof of Financial Means:** Bank statement (with an internationally accepted payment card if in a foreign currency) proving required monthly subsistence funds for study stays, or an official scholarship confirmation.
5. **Comprehensive Health Insurance (*Komplexní zdravotní pojištění cizinců*):** Required upon visa collection and throughout your entire stay in Czechia from an insurer licensed in the Czech Republic (e.g., **pVZP**, **Slavia**, **Maxima**, **UNIQA**, or **SV Pojišťovna**) with a statutory coverage limit of at least **EUR 400,000** per insured event without exclusions (pursuant to Czech Act No. 326/1999 Sb., § 180j).
6. **Criminal Record Extract (*Výpis z rejstříku trestů*):** Apostilled or superlegalized and officially translated into Czech.

title: Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules
text:
Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules

## 3. Post-Arrival Duties & Permit Extensions in Prague
- **3-Working-Day Foreign Police Registration:**
  - **VŠE Dormitories:** SÚZ VŠE reports your arrival to the Foreign Police **automatically** upon check-in.
  - **Private Accommodation:** Non-EU students must register in person within **3 working days** of arrival at the Prague Foreign Police (*Cizinecká policie*, Olšanská 2176/2, Prague 3 – Žižkov).
- **Biometrics Appointment (Long-Term Residence Permit):** Book an appointment online via the Official Information Portal for Foreigners / MOI Reservation System (https://frs.gov.cz/) to provide biometric data upon arrival and collect your biometric residence card.
- **Extending Your Permit:** Submit your renewal application to OAMP MVČR **between 120 days and 1 day before** your current visa or permit expires via https://frs.gov.cz/, attaching an updated VŠE Electronic Confirmation of Study (`/auth/student/potvrzeni.pl`), renewed Proof of Accommodation, proof of funds, and valid comprehensive health insurance.

title: Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules

Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – requirements and rules

## 4. EU / EEA / Swiss Students
- **No Visa Required:** Citizens of the EU, EEA, and Switzerland enter and study visa-free with a valid national ID card or passport.
- **30-Day Reporting Duty:** If staying in the Czech Republic for **more than 30 days**, EU/EEA/Swiss students must report their presence to the Foreign Police within 30 days of arrival—**unless staying in a VŠE dormitory**, which handles reporting automatically.
- **Health Coverage:** Bring a valid **European Health Insurance Card (EHIC)** and register it locally if needed.

## 2. Booking Your Visa Appointment & Timelines
- **UNVERIFIED (Dynamic External Schedules):** Individual Czech embassy visa appointment links, email registration windows, and quota rules change frequently and are not verified in real time. Always confirm directly on the website of your territorially competent Czech Embassy or Consulate via https://mzv.gov.cz/jnp/en/diplomatic_missions/index.html or with the VŠE International Office.
- **Book Early:** Statutory processing time for long-term study visas and residence permits is typically **up to 60 days** from the date a complete application is submitted at the embassy. title: Health insurance and medical care
text:
Health insurance and medical care

International students must have valid health insurance covering their stay in the Czech Republic. Two main categories:
- **EU/EEA/Swiss students**: use the **EHIC** (European Health Insurance Card) from your home country (registering it locally with a Czech public health insurance fund such as VZP ČR is recommended for full coverage).
- **Non-EU students**: must arrange **Comprehensive Health Insurance (*Komplexní zdravotní pojištění cizinců*)** with an insurance company licensed to operate in the Czech Republic (e.g. **pVZP**, **Slavia**, **Maxima**, **UNIQA**, or **SV Pojišťovna**) with a minimum coverage limit of **EUR 400,000** per insured event without exclusions (under Czech Act No. 326/1999 Sb., § 180j) as a mandatory condition of the long-stay visa or residence permit.

General practitioner (praktický lékař) and hospitals are accessible with valid insurance. Emergency: **155** (ambulance) or **112** (single European emergency number).

## Dormitory Locations and Campuses
VŠE offers student accommodation across multiple dormitories grouped primarily into two student campuses:
- **Jarov Campus (Prague 3 - Žižkov / Jarov):**
  - Palachova dormitory, Eislerova dormitory, Thalerova dormitory, University Hotel, and Jarov II.
  - Located approximately 10–15 minutes from the main VŠE campus in Žižkov by direct tram (lines 9, 26, 31 to tram stop Chmelnice or Strážní).
  - Very popular among degree students and international exchange students.
- **Jižní Město Campus (Prague 4 - Chodov / Kunratice):**
  - Blanice dormitory and Vltava dormitory.
  - Located directly at the Jižní Město satellite campus near metro line C (stations Chodov / Opatov) and bus stop Volha.
  - Houses both Czech and international students with dining halls and extensive outdoor sports areas nearby.
- **Other locations:** Rooseveltova dormitory (Prague 7 - Holešovice).

- **Grading scale at VŠE:**
  - 1 = Excellent (*Výborně*, 90–100%)
  - 2 = Very Good (*Velmi dobře*, 75–89%)
  - 3 = Good (*Dobře*, 60–74%)
  - 4+ = Conditional Fail with right to one retake during the active exam period (*Nevyhověl s možností opravy*, 50–59%)
  - 4 = Definitive Fail (*Nevyhověl*, under 50%)
  - Zápočet (z) = Satisfied / ungraded course requirement.

- **Exam retakes (`4+` / *Opravný termín*):** Under VŠE Study and Examination Regulations, students who earn a conditional fail of **`4+`** (50–59%) are entitled to **one retake date** within the same exam period (cannot be awarded twice in succession or on the last exam date of the period; an unused `4+` converts to `4`). title: Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE
text:
Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE

## What is Academic Psychological Counselling (APC)?
- Academic Psychological Counselling is a professional, confidential, and completely **free of charge** service provided by the Academic Centre (Akademické centrum) for all enrolled VŠE students and staff.
- **Languages Available:** Full counselling sessions are provided in **Czech** and **English** (Polish and Russian available upon specific request via email).
- **Format:** Consultations are conducted either in-person at the Žižkov campus or online via MS Teams, requiring prior reservation.

title: Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE
text:
Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE

## Common Reasons Students Seek Counselling
International students frequently consult the service for support with:
- **Academic adjustment and stress:** Overcoming exam anxiety, deadline pressure, procrastination, concentration difficulties, and loss of study motivation.
- **Culture shock and adaptation:** Coping with relocation to Prague, language barriers, loneliness, and homesickness.
- **Interpersonal relationships:** Communication difficulties with peers, roommates, professors, or partners.
- **Emotional and psychological well-being:** Mood fluctuations, chronic worry, mild depression, acute distress, or life transitions.
- **Personal and career development:** Self-confidence building, decision-making, and coping strategies.

title: Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE
text:
Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE

## How to Book an Appointment
1. **Check Schedule:** Review available consultation slots on the Academic Centre booking schedule at https://ac.vse.cz/english/psychological-counselling/opening-times/.
2. **Email Registration:** Write directly to `ac@vse.cz` indicating your student identification, faculty, and preferred language (English or Czech).
3. **Emergency Discretion:** If you are experiencing acute psychological distress, mention the urgency in the email subject line so the counsellors can prioritize your request.

title: Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE
text:
Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE

## Professional Ethics and Confidentiality
All counsellors adhere strictly to the Ethical Code of Czech University Counsellors:
- **Full Confidentiality:** Information shared during sessions is never disclosed to faculty administrators, professors, parents, or outside authorities.
- **Non-Judgmental Support:** Discretion, mutual respect, and student-centered support are unconditionally guaranteed.

title: Academic Psychological Counselling and Mental Well-being at VŠE
text:

## Urgent Mental Health Crisis & Emergency Helplines (24/7)
If you or someone you know is experiencing acute severe distress or a life-threatening mental health emergency, do not wait for a scheduled university appointment:
- **General Emergency (Police, Fire, Medical):** Dial **112** (available 24/7 in English and Czech, free of charge).
- **Czech Crisis Helpline (Linka první psychické pomoci):** Dial **116 123** (free, anonymous, available 24/7 for adults in psychological distress).
- **Safety Helpline (Linka bezpečí - for youth & students under 26):** Dial **116 111** (free, anonymous, 24/7).
- **Prague Crisis Intervention Centre (Centrum krizové intervence - Bohnice):**
  - Phone: `+420 284 016 110` (24/7 emergency psychiatric walk-in clinic and phone helpline).

text:
InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

## VŠE credit voucher system
- VŠE uses a virtual credit voucher system to measure study progress and allow flexibility.
- Each incoming student receives a voucher pool:
  - **Bachelor's students:** 216 vouchers (180 for standard degree requirements + 36 reserve vouchers = 20% safety margin).
  - **Master's students:** 144 vouchers (120 for standard degree requirements + 24 reserve vouchers = 20% safety margin).
- **How vouchers work:** 1 ECTS credit = 1 voucher. When enrolling in a course, the corresponding vouchers are deducted. Passing the course converts those vouchers into earned ECTS credits. Failing an enrolled course consumes the vouchers permanently without earning credits.
- If a student runs out of vouchers and has fewer vouchers remaining than ECTS needed to graduate, studies are terminated.

3. **Open Registration/Enrollment:** Click on **Registration/Enrollment** (Registrace/Zápisy).
4. **Browse Course Categories:** At the bottom of the page, click the course category indicator corresponding to your study plan:
   - `oP`: Major/programme compulsory courses (*povinné předměty*, Class I)
   - `sP` / `sV`: Minor specialization compulsory (`sP`, Class I) and selective (`sV`, Class II) courses
   - `fV`: Faculty and general free electives (*volitelné předměty*, Class II), plus language (`sJ`) and sports (`TV`) groups.

title: InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE
text:
InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

## Course registration and enrollment rounds
Registration in InSIS is split into clearly separated phases:
1. **Pre-registration (Orders):** Students express interest by ordering compulsory and elective courses. This phase is **not first-come, first-served**; submitting on day 1 or the final day gives equal priority.
2. **Automated processing:** InSIS allocates seats based on priority rules (curriculum requirements, earned credits, study plan group).
3. **Enrollment Round 1:** Management and confirmation of compulsory courses.
4. **Enrollment Round 2:** Enrollment of compulsory and pre-registered optional/elective courses.
5. **Enrollment Round 3 (Open changes):** Students can enroll in any open course across faculties that has remaining free capacity, even if not pre-registered.
6. **Add/Drop period:** Changes can still be made during the first week of teaching in the semester.

title: InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE
text:
InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

## Semester credit rules and exam retakes
- **Standard workload:** Standard full-time study load is **30 ECTS credits** per semester (60 ECTS per academic year).
- **First-semester thresholds:**
  - **Absolute minimum:** At least **9 ECTS credits** must be earned in the first semester to avoid immediate study termination by the Dean.
  - **Progression threshold:** At least **20 ECTS credits** should be earned to meet the cumulative `20 x active semesters` progression pace and prevent voucher deduction penalties.
- **Ongoing cumulative threshold:** In subsequent semesters, total earned credits must satisfy `Cumulative Credits >= 20 x number of active semesters` (e.g., 40 after semester 2, 60 after semester 3).
- **Exam retakes (`4+` rule):** Under VŠE Study and Examination Regulations, students who receive a conditional fail of **`4+`** (50–59%) are entitled to **one retake attempt** (*opravný termín*) within the same semester exam period (`4+` cannot be awarded twice in succession or on the last exam date, and an unused `4+` converts to `4`). Confirm course rules in the InSIS syllabus and with your Study Department.

## What is International Week (I-Week)?
- **Overview:** International Week (I-Week) is an intensive academic event organized by VŠE faculties (notably FIS, FPH, FIR) where visiting guest professors from top partner universities worldwide teach specialized courses in English.
- **Credits:** Each successfully completed International Week course awards **3 ECTS credits**.
- **Format and Schedule:** Unlike standard 13-week semester courses, I-Week courses are delivered in an intensive condensed block format over 3 to 4 days (e.g. Monday to Wednesday/Thursday with full-day interactive lectures, seminars, and a final group project or exam).
- **Attendance:** Due to the intensive format, 100% active attendance is mandatory across all scheduled sessions.
- **Target Audience:** Open to all degree students (Bachelor and Master across all VŠE faculties) as well as incoming international exchange/Erasmus students.

title: Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE
text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

## 1. Overview of Final Theses at VŠE
At VŠE (including the Faculty of Informatics and Statistics - FIS, and degree programmes like Information Systems Management - ISM), completing a Bachelor's or Master's programme requires writing, submitting, and defending a final thesis:
- **Bachelor’s Thesis (Bakalářská práce):** Recommended length approx. 10,000 words (around 35–50 standard pages).
- **Master’s / Diploma Thesis (Diplomová práce):** Recommended length approx. 20,000 words (around 60–80 standard pages).
- **Language:** Written in English for English-taught programmes (such as ISM, CEMS, MIMG, IBB, EDS) or Czech/Slovak for Czech programmes.
- **Templates:** Official VŠE templates (Word and LaTeX) with required ordering, APA citation styles, and title pages are available on the faculty website and InSIS.

title: Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE
text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

## 2. Thesis Topic Assignment (Zadání závěrečné práce)
1. **Topic Selection:** Choose an advertised topic in InSIS under **Student's Portal** → **Thesis Topics (Témata závěrečných prací)**, or agree on an individual research topic with a prospective supervisor (*vedoucí práce*).
2. **Assignment Protocol:** The supervisor enters the formal assignment into InSIS:
   - Official title in English and Czech.
   - Objectives and methodology (*Zásady pro vypracování*).
   - Preliminary table of contents and primary literature/sources.
3. **Approval:** The assignment is electronically approved in InSIS by the student, supervisor, head of department (*vedoucí katedry*), and dean/vice-dean. This must be completed well before final submission (typically 3–6 months in advance).

title: Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE
text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

## 3. Step-by-Step Electronic Thesis Submission in InSIS
Final theses at VŠE are submitted **electronically via InSIS**. Printed hard copies are generally no longer required for defense, unless specifically requested by your department.

title: Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE
text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

1. **Open InSIS:** Log in at https://insis.vse.cz/ with your VŠE credentials.
2. **Navigate to Submission Portal:** Go to **Student's Portal** (*Portál studenta*) → **Final Thesis** (*Závěrečná práce*).
3. **Fill Required Metadata:**
   - English and Czech thesis title (must match the approved assignment).
   - English and Czech abstract (*Abstrakt*).
   - English and Czech keywords (*Klíčová slova*).
4. **Upload Thesis File:**
   - Upload the full text of the thesis strictly in **PDF format** (searchable text, PDF/A standard recommended, no password protection).
   - The file must contain all formal sections: Title page, Declaration of Authorship / Originality, Table of Contents, Chapters, Reference List, and Appendices.
5. **Upload Supplementary Attachments:**
   - If your thesis involves practical software prototypes, code, datasets, or survey materials, package them into a `.zip` archive and upload under supplementary files.
6. **Confirm Final Submission:**
   - Click the final submission button (**Potvrdit odevzdání** / Confirm Submission).
   - Verify the system confirmation message: *"Elektronická verze závěrečné práce byla odevzdána a bylo potvrzeno její korektní vložení. Proces vkládání je tímto ukončen. Práci již nelze modifikovat."*
   - ⚠️ **Important Warning:** Once final submission is confirmed, the system locks your file. You cannot replace or edit the uploaded PDF directly.

title: Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE
text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

## 4. How to Submit Errata in InSIS (Errata k závěrečné práci)
If you discover factual errors, typos, calculation mistakes, or formatting inaccuracies **after** your thesis has already been locked and submitted in InSIS, you can submit an official **Errata** (*Errata k práci*):

### What is Errata?
Under the Higher Education Act (§ 47b) and VŠE Study Regulations, submitted theses become public academic records. An **Errata** (Erratum) is an official supplementary document listing specific corrections to errors identified in the submitted thesis without altering the locked original file.

Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

### How to Submit Errata in InSIS (Step-by-Step):
1. **Log in to InSIS:** Go to https://insis.vse.cz/.
2. **Access Final Thesis Application:** Navigate to **Student's Portal** (*Portál studenta*) → **Final Thesis** (*Závěrečná práce*).
3. **Find Errata Option:** In the student editing section (*Editační aplikace studenta*), locate the button **"Insert Errata"** (**Vložit errata**).
4. **Upload Errata File:** Upload your structured corrections document strictly in **PDF format**.
5. **Supervisor Consultation:** Always inform and consult your thesis supervisor (*vedoucí práce*) before uploading. The supervisor reviews the corrections and acknowledges them in InSIS.
6. **Publication:** Once confirmed, the Errata file is permanently attached to your final thesis record in InSIS and Theses.cz, making the corrections visible to the examination committee, opponent, and public readers.

title: Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE
text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

### Recommended Errata Document Format:
Prepare a clear 1–2 page PDF document structured as follows:
- **Header:**
  - University: Prague University of Economics and Business (VŠE)
  - Faculty and Programme (e.g. FIS – Information Systems Management)
  - Thesis Title: [Full Title of Your Thesis]
  - Author: [Your Full Name and Student ID]
  - Supervisor: [Supervisor's Name and Academic Titles]
  - Date: [Date of Errata Preparation]
- **Correction Table:**
  | Page / Section | Original (Erroneous) Text | Corrected (Accurate) Text | Reason / Note |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | Page 24, Table 2 | "Values in EUR thousands" | "Values in CZK thousands" | Unit label correction |
  | Page 48, Table 4 | "Value = 12.4%" | "Value = 18.2%" | Calculation adjustment |
- **Minor Errors at Defense:** For very minor typos or grammar glitches, you do not always need a formal Errata upload; you can prepare a brief slide in your defense presentation acknowledging the corrections in response to the opponent's review.

## 5. Automated Plagiarism Check (Theses.cz / VŠE Validator)
- After submission in InSIS, your thesis is automatically sent to the Czech national repository **Theses.cz** for similarity analysis against academic papers, published theses, and web pages.
- The similarity protocol is generated in InSIS within a few hours to days.
- Both your supervisor and opponent evaluate the similarity percentage and verify that all external sources and quotes are properly referenced according to academic ethics and VŠE AI guidelines.

text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

## 6. Supervisor and Opponent Reviews (Posudky)
- **Two Written Reviews:** Your thesis is evaluated independently by your supervisor (*Posudek vedoucího*) and an assigned opponent (*Posudek oponenta*).
- **Evaluation Criteria:** Fulfillment of thesis objectives, theoretical framework, methodology, analytical rigor, formal formatting, and original contribution.
- **Grade Proposal:** Both reviews propose a grade: *Výborně* (1 - Excellent), *Velmi dobře* (2 - Very Good), *Dobře* (3 - Good), or *Nevyhověl* (4 - Failed).
- **Questions for Defense:** The reviews include specific questions (*otázky k obhajobě*) which you must address during your defense presentation.
- **Deadline for Reviews:** Reviews must be published in InSIS at least **3 working days** before the defense date, giving you time to prepare your slides and answers.

text:
Final thesis submission, InSIS errata, defense and reviews at VŠE

## 7. Thesis Defense Presentation (Obhajoba)
1. **Prerequisites:** All required coursework and ECTS credits completed (180 ECTS for Bachelor, 120 ECTS for Master), thesis submitted on time.
2. **Registration:** Register for the defense date under **Student's Portal** → **State Final Exams (SZZ / Státnice)**.
3. **Presentation:** Prepare a 5–10 minute presentation (PowerPoint or PDF slides):
   - Background, motivation, and practical relevance.
   - Research questions / objectives.
   - Methodology and dataset / prototype implementation.
   - Key findings, evaluation metrics, and thesis contribution.
4. **Defense Procedure:**
   - Introduction of candidate and thesis title by the committee chair.
   - Student delivers the presentation.
   - Reading of the supervisor's and opponent's reviews.
   - Student presents direct, prepared answers to the review questions.
   - Open discussion and questions from committee members.
   - Closed committee deliberation and final grade announcement.

text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

> General summary grounded in the official VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ), Scholarship Regulations, SÚZ VŠE rules, and Czech immigration portals. Always verify binding rules with your faculty Study Department, International Office (OZS), or the responsible official authority.

title: VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations
text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

## Academic Regulations

### POL_001: Minimum 9 ECTS First-Semester Requirement
- **Summary:** Every newly admitted student must obtain at least 9 ECTS credits in their first semester to continue studying.
- **Details:** Pursuant to the VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ), a student must obtain a minimum of 9 ECTS credits (control credits) in their first semester of study. Failing to obtain at least 9 credits results in termination of study.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Termination of study by the Dean if fewer than 9 ECTS are earned in semester 1. Confirm details with your faculty Study Department.

title: VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations
text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

### POL_002: Cumulative Progression Requirement (20 ECTS per Active Semester)
- **Summary:** Students must maintain cumulative credit progress of at least 20 ECTS multiplied by the number of active semesters.
- **Details:** Under the VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ), students must maintain cumulative credit progress equal to at least 20 ECTS multiplied by the number of active (non-interrupted) semesters (for example, 40 ECTS after 2 semesters and 60 ECTS after 3 semesters). Falling short triggers credit voucher deductions or study termination if remaining vouchers fall below remaining required credits. Always confirm binding rules in the official SZŘ or with your faculty Study Department.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Credit voucher deduction equal to the shortfall; termination of study if remaining vouchers are insufficient to finish the degree.

title: VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations
text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

## Credit Vouchers & ECTS

### POL_003: Master's Credit Voucher Allocation (144 Vouchers)
- **Summary:** Master's students receive 144 credit vouchers to complete a 120 ECTS degree (24 reserve vouchers).
- **Details:** Master's degree students at VŠE are allocated 144 credit vouchers (120% of the 120 ECTS degree requirement) at initial enrollment. The 24 reserve vouchers provide a buffer for repeating failed courses or taking extra electives.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** If your remaining credit voucher balance drops below the remaining ECTS required to graduate, study is terminated.

text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

### POL_004: Bachelor's Credit Voucher Allocation (216 Vouchers)
- **Summary:** Bachelor's students receive 216 credit vouchers to complete a 180 ECTS degree (36 reserve vouchers).
- **Details:** Bachelor's degree students at VŠE are allocated 216 credit vouchers (120% of the 180 ECTS degree requirement) to complete their study plan. The 36 reserve vouchers provide flexibility for repeating failed courses or taking additional electives.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Exhausting credit vouchers below remaining degree ECTS prevents graduation and results in study termination.

title: VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations
text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

### POL_005: Voucher Consumption for Failed Courses
- **Summary:** Enrolling in a course deducts credit vouchers equal to its ECTS value; failing the course does not refund those vouchers.
- **Details:** One ECTS credit equals one credit voucher. Vouchers are deducted upon course enrollment in InSIS. Passing converts them into earned ECTS credits; receiving a final grade of 4 (Fail) consumes those vouchers permanently, so repeating the course consumes a fresh set of vouchers from your reserve pool.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Permanent loss of reserve vouchers, increasing risk of falling below the required graduation voucher threshold.

title: VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations
text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

## Academic Regulations

### POL_006: Mandatory Re-enrollment of Failed Compulsory Courses
- **Summary:** A failed compulsory (oP) course must be re-enrolled in the next semester it is offered; failing it a second time terminates studies.
- **Details:** Under VŠE Study and Examination Regulations, a failed compulsory course (oP — povinný předmět) must be re-registered in the next offered semester. Elective courses (fV faculty/free electives or sV minor electives) do not have to be repeated — an alternative eligible elective may be selected instead. A compulsory course can be enrolled at most twice.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Failing a compulsory course on its second enrollment results in termination of study. Always confirm options with your faculty Study Department.

VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

### POL_007: Interruption of Studies (Přerušení studia)
- **Summary:** Students may apply to interrupt studies via InSIS; non-EU students face immediate residence-permit implications.
- **Details:** Students who meet first-semester credit requirements (or face documented serious medical, personal, or parental reasons) may request study interruption (přerušení studia) through InSIS Contact Centre / Document Office. During interruption, student status is suspended. Always verify permitted duration and conditions in the VŠE SZŘ and with your faculty Study Department.
- **Official Reference:** Czech Higher Education Act No. 111/1998 Sb. § 54; VŠE SZŘ (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Non-EU visa/residence permit holders lose active study status during interruption and must consult the VŠE International Office and MOI (ipc.gov.cz) beforehand.

VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

### POL_008: Recognition of Courses & Credits from Prior Studies
- **Summary:** Courses completed in previous studies with grade 1 (Excellent), grade 2 (Very Good), or Credited (započteno) may be considered for recognition.
- **Details:** Students may apply via InSIS for recognition of equivalent university courses previously completed with Czech grade 1 (Excellent), grade 2 (Very Good), or Credited (započteno). Grade 3 (Good) is generally not eligible for recognition. Exact time limits (commonly 3 calendar years for prior VŠE studies) and credit-transfer rules depend on your faculty Dean's Directive — verify with your faculty Study Department.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ); Faculty Directives (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Courses graded 3 (Good) or exceeding the faculty's eligibility window are not recognized.

### POL_009: Minor Specialization (Vedlejší specializace) Policy
- **Summary:** Selected VŠE Master's curricula include a 30 ECTS Minor Specialization, depending on the specific programme study plan.
- **Details:** Standard Czech Master's curricula and selected programmes at VŠE include a Minor Specialization (vedlejší specializace, course groups sP/sV) typically comprising 30 ECTS and a comprehensive minor exam. Requirements vary for English-taught Master's programmes (such as ISM), so verify whether a minor specialization applies in InSIS Check of Study Plan or with your faculty Study Department.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ); Faculty Curricula (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Where required by the programme curriculum, failure to complete the minor specialization blocks graduation.

text:
VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

## Examination & Grading

### POL_010: VŠE Grading Scale & 4+ Conditional Retake Rule
- **Summary:** VŠE grades 1 (90–100%), 2 (75–89%), 3 (60–74%), 4+ (50–59%, conditional fail granting one retake), and 4 (<50%, definitive fail).
- **Details:** Under the VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ), courses are graded: 1 = Výborně (Excellent, 90–100%), 2 = Velmi dobře (Very Good, 75–89%), 3 = Dobře (Good, 60–74%), 4+ = Nevyhověl s možností opravy (Fail with right to one retake examination during the active exam period, typically 50–59%), and 4 = Nevyhověl (Definitive Fail, below 50%). Key restrictions on 4+: (1) 4+ cannot be awarded twice in succession for the same course, (2) 4+ cannot be awarded on the last exam date of the period because no retake date remains, and (3) an unused 4+ automatically converts to 4 at the end of the exam period. Confirm course-specific assessment rules in the InSIS syllabus and with your faculty Study Department.
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** A definitive grade 4 yields 0 ECTS and permanently consumes the spent credit vouchers. A failed compulsory course (oP) must be re-enrolled in the next offered semester; failing a compulsory course twice terminates study.

### POL_011: Exam Deregistration & Unexcused Absence in InSIS
- **Summary:** Cancel exam registrations in InSIS before the published deadline; unexcused absence results in Grade 4 (Fail).
- **Details:** Students registered for an examination date in InSIS may withdraw without penalty prior to the closing deadline set by the examiner in InSIS. Failing to attend a registered exam without timely deregistration or an accepted medical/serious excuse submitted via InSIS Contact Centre / Study Department results in grade 4 (Fail).
- **Official Reference:** VŠE Study and Examination Regulations (SZŘ) (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Automatic Grade 4 (Fail); confirm medical excuse submission windows with your faculty Study Department.

VŠE Core Study Policies, Credit Vouchers & Institutional Regulations

## Academic Integrity

### POL_012: Theses.cz Plagiarism Check, AI Disclosure & Disciplinary Code
- **Summary:** All final theses are checked via Theses.cz; Generative AI usage must comply with VŠE ethics guidelines and be transparently disclosed.
- **Details:** Every final thesis uploaded in InSIS is automatically scanned by the national anti-plagiarism repository Theses.cz. Any use of Generative AI tools in coursework or theses must adhere to current VŠE and faculty guidelines and be transparently disclosed; submitting unacknowledged AI-generated work or plagiarized material is academic misconduct adjudicated by the Faculty Disciplinary Commission under Act No. 111/1998 Sb. § 64–65 (sanctions: reprimand, conditional expulsion, or expulsion).
- **Official Reference:** Act No. 111/1998 Sb. § 64–65; VŠE Ethical & Thesis Guidelines (https://www.vse.cz/english/students/study/study-regulations/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Referral to the Faculty Disciplinary Commission, up to permanent expulsion from VŠE.

## Final Thesis & State Exams

### POL_013: Electronic Thesis Submission (PDF/A), Bilingual Abstracts & § 47b Errata
- **Summary:** Theses are submitted electronically in InSIS (PDF/A + English/Czech abstracts and keywords); post-submission corrections use official § 47b Errata.
- **Details:** VŠE operates electronic thesis submission in InSIS (Student's Portal -> Final Thesis, /auth/student/zp.pl). Before locking submission, students must enter both English and Czech abstracts and keywords and upload the thesis in searchable PDF/A format (plus optional ZIP appendices). Once confirmed, the thesis file is immutable under Czech Higher Education Act § 47b; any factual or typographical corrections discovered after locking must be uploaded as a separate Errata PDF via 'Insert errata' (Vložit errata) in consultation with your supervisor. Supervisor and opponent reviews are published in InSIS ahead of the defense.
- **Official Reference:** Act No. 111/1998 Sb. § 47b; VŠE Thesis & InSIS Guidelines (https://vskp.vse.cz/english)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Missing English/Czech metadata blocks InSIS submission; locked theses cannot be overwritten directly.

## Visa, Health & Wellbeing

### POL_018: Foreign Police Registration, Health Insurance & Free VŠE Psychological Counselling
- **Summary:** Non-EU students report to Foreign Police within 3 working days (EU >30 days within 30 days in private flats); comprehensive insurance is mandatory for non-EU; AC VŠE counselling is free.
- **Details:** Under Czech Act No. 326/1999 Sb. § 93, non-EU nationals must report their place of residence to the Foreign Police (Cizinecká policie) within 3 working days of arrival, and EU nationals staying longer than 30 days in private flats must report within 30 days (VŠE dormitory residents are registered automatically by SÚZ VŠE). Non-EU students must maintain valid comprehensive Czech health insurance from an authorized insurer throughout their stay (EU students carry EHIC). Always verify binding immigration and insurance requirements on https://ipc.gov.cz/en/ and with the VŠE International Office (OZS). For stress, anxiety, or homesickness, Academic Psychological Counselling (AC VŠE, ac@vse.cz) offers free, confidential sessions in English and Czech.
- **Official Reference:** Act No. 326/1999 Sb. § 93; MOI (ipc.gov.cz); AC VŠE (ac.vse.cz) (https://ipc.gov.cz/en/)
- **Consequences / Notes:** Failure to report presence or maintain valid insurance carries immigration penalties. AC VŠE counselling is 100% confidential and never reported to faculties.
